summary: OUTPOST ZERO is an interactive educational survival game designed for children aged 7–12. Players take command of a lunar outpost and must keep four astronauts alive for 30 simulated days. They manage essential resources, including oxygen, electricity, food and radiation protection, while responding to unexpected space events and communication delays. Every decision involves a trade-off, teaching players how real astronauts and mission planners balance limited resources, safety and scientific exploration. Inspired by NASA's space exploration research, OUTPOST ZERO makes the challenges of living beyond Earth engaging, educational and interactive.
details: OUTPOST ZERO is an educational lunar survival simulation designed for children aged 7–12, where players take the role of an outpost commander responsible for keeping four astronauts alive for 30 simulated days. Players must manage essential resources such as oxygen, electricity, food and radiation protection while responding to challenges like solar storms, equipment failures and communication delays with Earth. The game focuses on realistic engineering trade-offs, where every decision has consequences, teaching players the importance of resource management, critical thinking, problem-solving and astronaut safety. Inspired by real NASA space exploration research, the project aims to make complex scientific concepts accessible, interactive and engaging while inspiring young people to explore science, technology, engineering and space exploration. Canva was used to develop the project's visual presentation, promotional demonstration video and poster, while HTML, CSS and JavaScript are proposed technologies for developing the interactive browser-based experience. Our team prioritised scientific relevance, educational value, age-appropriate gameplay, accessibility and creativity to demonstrate the challenges of sustaining human life beyond Earth.
